stem: For which word, the letter 'G' has been used in '2G Spectrum'?
expl: 2G is the second generation of wireless communication technology. In 2G spectrum, the letter ‘G’ is used for “Generation”, i.e., “second generation”.

expl: The quality of a printer is determined by “dots per inch”. It is expressed as dpi (dots per inch).

stem:

1. Cobra

stem: Which one of the following is not the language of computer?
expl: BASIC, C and FORTRAN are computer languages, but FAST is not a computer language.

stem:
Which of the following technologies will be enabled by the 5G mobile communication networks?
1. Internet of Things
2. Edge Computing
3. Network Slicing
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
expl: 5G (fifth generation) is the latest mobile communication technology, through which the use of technologies and devices such as the Internet of Things (IoT), edge computing, network slicing, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, etc. will become easier. IoT (Internet of Things) is a network that connects those objects which are capable of storing and transforming data. Edge computing is an extension of cloud computing, in which data is analyzed at the local level.

stem: What is the full form of GPT in ChatGPT, recently seen in the news?
expl: ChatGPT is an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based language model. It has been developed by OpenAI. It is capable of understanding and responding in human-like language. The full form of GPT is—Generative Pre-trained Transformer.

stem: Name of the first 3D printed humanoid robot in India is :
expl: ‘Manav’ is India’s first indigenous 3D (three-dimensional) printed humanoid robot. Manav is a two-foot-tall humanoid robot and looks like a big toy. It has 21 sensors. There are two cameras in its eye sockets and two microphones on both sides of its head. This robot, made by Diwakar Vaish, was unveiled at IIT Bombay Techfest 2014–2015.

stem: What is true of the GSLV-F15 mission by ISRO?

options.label: b
options.text: It marked ISRO's 101st launch from Sriharikota

options.label: c
options.text: It marked ISRO's 100th launch from Sriharikota

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: On 29 January 2025, ISRO launched GSLV-F15 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, as the 100th launch mission from Sriharikota. Through this launch vehicle, the NVS-02 navigation satellite for the NavIC system was placed into a Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). The launch and satellite injection into GTO were successful; however, during the later orbit-raising process, the oxidizer valve did not open. Therefore, the satellite could not reach the intended geosynchronous orbit and remained in an elliptical orbit. Now it is not operational. Since both options (a) and (c) are correct, the correct answer is option (d).

stem: Who was the inventor of RADAR?
expl: Scottish physicist Robert Watson developed the first experimental radar (RADAR—Radio Detection and Ranging) system in 1935. During World War II, this system was used to give warning before air attacks.

stem: Sir C.V. Raman received Nobel Prize for physics in the year :
expl: Dr. Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman was the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize in Physics. He received this award in 1930.

stem: Raman effect is due to Sir C.V. Raman. Which of the following statements is correct about the 'Raman effect'?

options.label: a
options.text: The Raman effect is an example of elastic scattering of light.

options.label: b
options.text: The frequency of scattered light increases and decreases after scattering.

options.label: c
options.text: The frequency of incident light can only decrease after scattering.

expl: In elastic scattering of light, the frequency of the photon remains unchanged; however, in the Raman effect, the frequency of light after scattering may increase or decrease.

stem: Einstein got the Nobel Prize for :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Albert Einstein was honoured for his services to theoretical physics, especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect. He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for 1921, and he received the prize in 1922.

stem: Name the scientist who said that matter can be converted into energy—

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Einstein explained that mass and energy are not two separate forms; they can be converted into each other. In this context, he established a relation between mass and energy, known as Einstein’s mass–energy equation. According to this, mass (matter) can be converted into energy, and energy can again be converted into mass. E = mc²; Where E is energy, m is mass, and c is the speed of light.

stem: Who was the scientist who discovered the telescope?
expl: The telescope was invented by Galileo.

stem: Who invented the aeroplane at the beginning of this century?
expl: The Wright Brothers invented the aeroplane.
